problem_restatements: Channel inversion problem: each prime p defines a discrete memoryless channel mapping integers to residue classes. The network must learn the channel transition function for 9 channels from a shared representation.

Sufficient statistic compression under multi-receiver constraints: the input (a,b) contains log2(max(a+b)) bits but only log2(p) bits are relevant for prime p. The network must learn to discard quotient bits and retain residue bits simultaneously for all 9 primes.
analogy: Syndrome decoding in error-correcting codes combined with successive refinement from broadcast channel theory. The remainder (a+b) mod p IS the syndrome of (a+b) under the cyclic code generated by p. Each prime defines a different code with different parity-check structure.

ops: parity_accumulator: ReLU(W_acc * (e_a + e_b) + b_acc) — extracts the sum as sufficient statistic; element-wise embedding addition preserves additive structure

successive_refinement_compressor: h through three bottleneck stages of increasing dimension (32, 64, 128) with skip connections — forces multi-resolution compression; small primes decode from coarse level, large primes need full resolution
syndrome_basis_synthesizer: for each residue class k under prime p, generates matched-filter basis vector using prime embedding and harmonic coordinates [cos(2*pi*k/p), sin(2*pi*k/p), ...]
syndrome_correlator: score_k = h_full dot v_k — matched-filter detection via inner product, zero learned parameters
iterative_belief_refiner: feeds scores back to refine representation, repeated T=2 times — inspired by iterative belief propagation in turbo decoding
plan.composition_strategy: parallel paths merge at correlation step, followed by feedback loop
plan.layer_arrangement: L1: embed(a,b,p). L2: parity_accumulator(e_a+e_b). L3: successive_refinement_compressor -> h_full. L4: syndrome_basis_synthesizer(p,k) for each k. L5: syndrome_correlator(h_full, v_k). L6: iterative_belief_refiner(scores->delta->recompute), T=2 iterations.
plan.reasoning: mod IS syndrome computation — Z -> Z/pZ is the syndrome map for repetition code with generator p. Successive refinement prevents memorization through bottleneck. Iterative feedback provides nonlinearity for piecewise-linear mod function.

expected_outcome: Test accuracy 70-85%, substantially above 45.3% baseline. Small primes near 90%+, large primes 60-70%. Much smaller train-test gap due to bottleneck preventing memorization. ~120k parameters.
falsification: If test accuracy below 55%: syndrome approach fails to capture modular structure. If syndrome basis vectors not approximately orthogonal: synthesizer failing. If removing compressor improves accuracy: bottleneck hypothesis wrong.
look_back: Z -> Z/pZ is literally the syndrome map for a repetition code — structural identity, not metaphor.
Successive refinement elegantly solves multi-prime challenge without per-prime components.
Generalizes beyond addition: replacing parity_accumulator enables other modular operations.
Potential weakness: harmonic coordinates might shortcut rather than enable genuine learning.
